questions.0.explain.t: DAST is black box: it sends requests and observes the responses of the running application.

questions.0.options.0.t: Reading the application's source code line by line, looking for insecure patterns

questions.0.options.1.t: By attacking the running application from the outside, like a malicious user

questions.0.options.2.t: Comparing library versions with a database of known CVEs

questions.0.options.3.t: Reviewing the architecture diagram to find dangerous flows

questions.1.explain.t: Active scans fire attack payloads; in staging the impact is contained.

questions.1.options.0.t: Because it only works with test databases that are empty

questions.1.options.1.t: Because the tests can create data, cause slowness or side effects

questions.1.options.2.t: Because production does not accept HTTP requests from external tools

questions.1.options.3.t: Because DAST cannot test applications that use HTTPS

questions.1.q.t: Why does DAST usually run in staging and not directly in production?

questions.2.explain.t: The two complement each other: SAST looks at the code, DAST looks at the live system.

questions.2.options.0.t: Variables declared and never used in the code

questions.2.options.1.t: Configuration problems and runtime behavior (headers, TLS, authentication)

questions.2.options.2.t: The technical debt built up in the codebase over the years

questions.2.options.3.t: The licenses of the dependencies used by the application

questions.2.q.t: What does DAST see that SAST normally does not?
